etymologies.etymologyHTML: Related to how quiet the shoes are. sneak +‎ -er

quote.citation: 1823, Elia [pseudonym; Charles Lamb], Elia. Essays which have Appeared under that Signature in The London Magazine, London:  […]  [Thomas Davison] for Taylor and Hessey, […], →OCLC:
quote.text: Beshrew the man who on such a day as this, the general festival, should affect to stand aloof. I am none of those sneakers. I am free of the corporation, and care not who knows it.

definitions.definition: (US, Atlantic Canada, Australia, New Zealand) An athletic shoe with a soft, rubber sole. A trainer.
(UK, dialect, archaic) A vessel of drink.

quote.text: I have just left the right worshipful and his myrmidons about a sneaker of five gallons!

definitions.definition: (India, archaic) A large cup (or small basin) with a saucer and cover.

quote.citation: 2008, Faye Flam, The Score: The Science of the Male Sex Drive‎[1]:
quote.text: These sneakers may go on this way indefinitely, or, if one of the big males somehow dies or disappears, a sneaker male's hormones will trigger a huge growth spurt and he'll metamorphose into an alpha male.
